deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is a register of the members of the Prussian order 'Pour le Mérite für Wissenschaften und Künste', founded by Friedrich Wilhelm IV in 1842. The heading 'O. p. l. m' stands for 'Orden pour le mérite'. Gauss was a founding member and lists himself as 'F. Gauss'.

Left column: the German (domestic) members.
- Scholars and scientists, 22 names in alphabetical blocks separated by rules: Bessel, Boeckh, Bopp, L. v. Buch, Dieffenbach, Eichhorn, Ehrenberg, Encke, Gauss, J. Grimm | A. v. Humboldt, C. G. J. Jacobi, Metternich, Mitscherlich, Joh. Müller, C. Ritter, Rückert, Savigny, Schelling, A. W. v. Schlegel | Schönlein, Tieck.
- Artists, 8 names: P. v. Cornelius, C. F. Lessing (Düsseldorf), Mendelssohn Bartholdy, Meyerbeer, Rauch, Schadow, Schnorr v. Carolsfeld, Schwanthaler (München).
- The total is 30, the statutory number of domestic members.

Right column: the foreign members.
- Scholars and scientists, 17 names: Arago, Avellino, Berzelius, Borghesi, Rob. Brown, Chateaubriand, Faraday, Fossombroni, Gay-Lussac, John Herschel | Zhukovsky, Kopitar, Krusenstern, Letronne, Melloni, Thomas Moore, Oersted.
- Artists, 8 names: Daguerre, Fontaine, Ingres, Liszt, Rossini, Thorvaldsen, Toschi, Horace Vernet.
- The total is 25.
- Later elections are appended below: Spontini, Oehlenschläger, Manzoni, Endlicher, Kunth, Spohr, Gottfried Hermann.

Gauss kept the list up to date with death marks (†). Some carry dates: Bessel 1846 März 17; Berzelius 1848 Aug 7; Dieffenbach 1847 Nov; Schlegel 1845 Mai 12; Mendelssohn 1847 Nov; Schwanthaler 1848 Nov 15. Buch carries a year only (1853). Others carry a bare †: Chateaubriand, Gay-Lussac (1850), Jacobi (1851), Tieck (1853), Thorwaldsen. The latest dated entry is 1853, so the annotations run up to about 1853.

The neighbouring pages are unrelated: income tables on the previous page; widow-pension and magnetic-inclination notes on the next page.
errors: Schwanthaler's death is usually given as 14 November 1848; Gauss writes Nov 15 (possibly a report date).
Several members who died early are not marked †: Fossombroni (d. 1844), Kopitar (d. 1844), Krusenstern (d. 1846). The list of deaths is therefore incomplete, not wrong.
The other dated deaths check out: Bessel 17 Mar 1846, Berzelius 7 Aug 1848, Dieffenbach 11 Nov 1847, Schlegel 12 May 1845, Mendelssohn 4 Nov 1847, L. v. Buch 4 Mar 1853.

results.what: Membership list of the order Pour le Mérite für Wissenschaften und Künste (founding members from 1842 plus later elections), annotated with deaths

deep.surprise_reason: This is a non-mathematical list of order members. Gauss's membership since 1842 is well known, and the page contains no mathematical content.

checkable.asserts: The domestic list has 22 scholars plus 8 artists, giving the statutory 30 domestic members.
The original foreign list has 17 scholars plus 8 artists, giving 25 before the later additions.

transcription_corrections: A pencil folio number '50' precedes 'O. p. l. m'.
'J. Meierbeer' is Gauss's spelling of Meyerbeer; 'Fr. Lisst' is his spelling of Liszt; 'G. Schaddow' may read with a double d. These are faithful to the manuscript.
'M. Schwanthaler zu München' is more exactly 'M. Schwanthaler', with 'z. München' written above and '1848 † Nov 15' below.
'Rob. Brown (London)' is fine; 'London' is underlined in brackets.
'J. v. Schelling' should read 'J. v. Schelling' / 'F. W. J. v. Schelling' (the 'J.' is as written).
